articles.title: Em dia de nervosismo no mercado, Tesouro Nacional recompra R$ 7,1 bilhões em títulos públicos | G1
articles.standfirst: Leilões de recompra foram realizados um dia após a vitória de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) nas eleições presidenciais, algo que surpreendeu e gerou tensão no mercado financeiro.
articles.summary: Leilões de recompra foram realizados um dia após a vitória de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) nas eleições presidenciais, algo que surpreendeu e gerou tensão no mercado financeiro.
articles.body:
A Secretaria do Tesouro Nacional realizou nesta segunda-feira (26) a recompra de títulos públicos no valor de R$ 7,1 bilhões. Foram realizadas três operações.

Os leilões de recompra foram realizados um dia após a vitória de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) nas eleições presidenciais , algo que surpreendeu e gerou tensão no mercado financeiro.

Na retomada dos negócios, voltou com um recuo de mais de 17%. Perto das 12h, caía 15,81%, aos 172.669 pontos.

Além disso, o dólar opera em alta, com um avanço de 9,29% perto das 12h, cotado a R$ 5,4568. Na máxima do dia, chegou a R$ 5,6048.

Ao recomprar títulos públicos, o Tesouro reduz a quantidade de papéis em circulação e ajuda a aumentar a liquidez do mercado, contribuindo para um funcionamento mais ordenado das negociações em momentos de maior turbulência.

Após a confirmação do resultado das eleições, parte dos investidores passou a exigir taxas de juros mais elevadas para financiar a dívida pública brasileira, o que reflete o aumento das incertezas sobre o cenário econômico e fiscal.

Como os preços dos títulos se movem em direção oposta às taxas de juros, essa reavaliação tende a provocar oscilações mais intensas nas cotações negociadas no mercado secundário.

Nesse contexto, as operações de recompra podem ajudar a reduzir movimentos abruptos de preços e a preservar a liquidez dos papéis.

articles.title: Ibovespa desaba após reeleição de Lula e ações recuam até 58%; veja as maiores quedas | G1
articles.standfirst: A bolsa acionou o circuit breaker após cair mais de 10% no início do pregão; ações ligadas ao consumo e ao mercado doméstico recuaram mais, enquanto exportadoras como Suzano e Vale subiram.
articles.summary: A bolsa acionou o circuit breaker após cair mais de 10% no início do pregão; ações ligadas ao consumo e ao mercado doméstico recuaram mais, enquanto exportadoras como Suzano e Vale subiram.
articles.body:
A bolsa brasileira teve um pregão de forte turbulência nesta segunda-feira (26), após a reeleição de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT). O Ibovespa , principal índice da B3 , caiu mais de 10% nos primeiros minutos de negociação e acionou o circuit breaker.

No fechamento do dia, o índice caiu 13,88% , aos 176.608 pontos . A reação refletiu a surpresa de parte dos investidores com o resultado das urnas e a revisão das expectativas para a condução da política econômica, os juros e as contas públicas .

Entre as ações com maiores perdas, Magazine Luiza liderou a lista, com queda de 58,23% , seguida por Vamos (-56,79%) e Hapvida (-54,93%). Papéis de empresas ligadas ao consumo, ao varejo e ao mercado imobiliário também registravam baixas expressivas. ( veja as dez maiores quedas abaixo )

“O pregão desta segunda-feira foi marcado por extrema volatilidade e forte aversão ao risco no mercado financeiro brasileiro, refletindo a reprecificação dos ativos após a definição do cenário político”, afirma Rebecca Nossig, estrategista de ações da Nomad.

🔎 Circuit breaker é um mecanismo utilizado pela bolsa para interromper temporariamente as negociações quando o mercado de ações registra quedas muito bruscas. O objetivo é dar tempo para que os investidores reavaliem suas decisões e reduzir o risco de movimentos desordenados de compra e venda. Após a interrupção, os negócios são retomados. Saiba mais .

As 10 maiores quedas do Ibovespa em 26 de outubro — Foto: Arte/g1

A onda de perdas na bolsa atingiu também algumas das maiores empresas do mercado brasileiro, cujas ações têm peso relevante no Ibovespa.

Conhecidos como “blue chips” , esses papéis incluem os de grandes bancos, da Petrobras e da Vale, mas tiveram desempenhos diferentes no pregão desta segunda-feira.

Entre os bancos, o Banco do Brasil registrou a maior queda, de 27,31% . As ações preferenciais do Bradesco recuaram 21,70%, enquanto as ordinárias caíram 20,65%. O BTG Pactual perdeu 24,83% , e o Itaú Unibanco teve baixa de 13,66%.

A Petrobras também fechou em queda, com recuo de 8,18% nas ações preferenciais e de 6,81% nas ordinárias.

👉 O desempenho dessas empresas tem impacto importante sobre o Ibovespa, principal índice da bolsa brasileira, porque cada ação tem um peso diferente em sua composição. Quanto maior essa participação, maior a influência da variação do papel sobre o resultado do indicador.

Dólar favorece exportadoras em dia de turbulência

Entre as ações que fecharam em alta nesta segunda-feira, a Suzano teve um dos melhores desempenhos, com valorização de 10,08%. A Embraer subiu 8,89%, a WEG avançou 5,10%, e a Klabin ganhou 3,24%. A Vale também encerrou o pregão no positivo, com alta de 4,01%.

Parte desse desempenho pode ser explicada pela alta do dólar, que encerrou o dia com alta de 8,21%, cotado a R$ 5,4027. Na sexta-feira (23), a moeda americana estava cotada a R$ 4,99 .

Segundo João Daronco, analista da Suno Research, empresas que recebem parte de suas receitas em moeda estrangeira podem se beneficiar quando a cotação da moeda americana sobe, já que esses valores, convertidos em reais, passam a representar mais dinheiro.

Ele destaca Vale, Klabin e Suzano como exemplos de companhias que tiveram desempenho positivo durante o pregão.

“Com a alta substancial do dólar e a perspectiva de que ele continue subindo, essas companhias conseguem diluir o custo fixo e melhorar suas margens”, afirmou.

Apenas 8 ações fecharam em alta nesta segunda-feira (26) — Foto: Arte/g1

O movimento, porém, não favorece todas as empresas. Daronco também destacou o impacto da alta dos juros futuros sobre companhias mais endividadas.

Com a revisão das expectativas para a economia, as taxas de juros de longo prazo subiram, o que pode encarecer o financiamento e prejudicar empresas que dependem de crédito. Essas companhias vinham se beneficiando de condições de financiamento mais favoráveis.

Para Daronco, as oscilações devem continuar nos próximos dias e semanas, enquanto o mercado avalia os desdobramentos do resultado eleitoral. Diante desse cenário, o analista recomenda cautela.

“Em dias como este, muitas vezes, o melhor é não se mexer”, disse.

articles.title: Goleiro Miguel Meneses do São José está na UTI; clube pede sangue | G1
articles.standfirst: Miguel Meneses, de 14 anos, sofreu um acidente de trânsito no Anel Viário de São José dos Campos, no domingo (25); clube pede que doadores informem o nome do atleta.
articles.summary: Miguel Meneses, do sub-15 do São José, sofreu acidente no Anel Viário e está internado; doações de sangue devem ser feitas no Banco de Sangue da cidade.
articles.body:
Goleiro Miguel Meneses, do sub-15 São José. — Foto: Reprodução/Assessoria do SJEC

O goleiro Miguel Meneses, de 14 anos, da equipe sub-15 do São José Esporte Clube, está internado na Unidade de Terapia Intensiva (UTI) após sofrer um grave acidente de trânsito no último domingo (25), no Anel Viário de São José dos Campos (SP).

O clube fez um apelo por doações de sangue para ajudar o atleta e pediu a colaboração da torcida joseense e de toda a população (leia mais abaixo). Segundo informações da Polícia Militar, o acidente aconteceu por volta das 16h15 de domingo (25), na altura do Monte Castelo, no Mirante do Anel Viário, em São José dos Campos.

De acordo com a corporação, o motorista de um Honda Civic perdeu o controle da direção ao passar por uma curva e bateu contra uma árvore no canteiro da via. No momento do acidente, chovia e a pista estava molhada.

Quatro pessoas estavam no veículo, todas da mesma família. As quatro sofreram ferimentos graves e foram encaminhadas ao pronto-socorro da Vila Industrial.

Entre as vítimas estava o goleiro Miguel Meneses Fernandes Vieira, jogador da equipe sub-15 do São José Esporte Clube. Ele foi socorrido por uma unidade de suporte avançado.

Ainda segundo a Polícia Militar, devido à gravidade da ocorrência e à necessidade de atendimento urgente, não foi possível colher os depoimentos das vítimas no local.

As doações podem ser feitas no Banco de Sangue de São José dos Campos, de segunda a sexta-feira, das 7h às 16h, sem necessidade de agendamento.

No momento da doação, é necessário informar que o sangue é destinado ao atleta Miguel Meneses. Também é preciso apresentar um documento original com foto.

O Banco de Sangue fica na Rua Antônio Saes, 425, no Centro de São José dos Campos. O estacionamento está localizado na Rua Antônio Saes, 449.

Goleiro Gabriel Meneses, do sub-15 do São José. — Foto: Reprodução/assessoria SJEC

O Hemocentro de São José dos Campos informou que o estoque de sangue do tipo O+ está com 216 bolsas disponíveis no começo da tarde desta segunda-feira (26), o equivalente a 70% da capacidade informada, de 306 bolsas.

Já o estoque do tipo O- foi normalizado. Segundo o Hemocentro, os demais tipos sanguíneos estão com os estoques dentro do necessário.

articles.title: Circuit breaker: relembre as vezes que a Bolsa parou desde 1997 | G1
articles.standfirst: Mecanismo é acionado quando o Ibovespa registra quedas de 10%, 15% ou 20%, com interrupções que podem durar de 30 minutos a mais de uma hora. Relembre quando a medida já foi usada no Brasil.
articles.summary: Mecanismo é acionado quando o Ibovespa registra quedas de 10%, 15% ou 20%, com interrupções que podem durar de 30 minutos a mais de uma hora. Relembre quando a medida já foi usada
articles.body:
Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) foi reeleito presidente da República neste domingo (25) e governará o Brasil por mais quatro anos. Com a vitória do petista e a derrota de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) nas urnas, o mercado financeiro passou esta segunda-feira (26) no vermelho, chegando a registrar queda de 16,48% e acionando o circuit breaker — algo que não acontecia desde o início da pandemia de Covid-19 no Brasil, em 2020.

🔎 O circuit breaker é um mecanismo de segurança da Bolsa de Valores brasileira (B3) que interrompe temporariamente as negociações quando o Ibovespa registra quedas muito acentuadas. O objetivo é conter movimentos de pânico no mercado financeiro e dar tempo para que os investidores reavaliem suas decisões.

Naquela ocasião, o coronavírus avançava rapidamente pelo país, os primeiros óbitos pela doença começavam a ser registrados e estados e municípios começavam a adotar medidas de isolamento social para tentar conter a disseminação do vírus.

Com toda a incerteza que pairava sob a pandemia e a economia global, o mercado financeiro protagonizou uma debandada do Ibovespa, resultando em uma queda vertiginosa.

Ao todo, o mecanismo foi acionado 6 vezes na pandemia:

9 de março : o mecanismo foi acionado pela primeira vez naquele ano, após o Ibovespa despencar mais de 10% durante o pregão.

11 de março : no mesmo dia em que a Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS) declarou oficialmente a pandemia de Covid-19, a Bolsa brasileira voltou a interromper as negociações após uma queda acentuada.

12 de março : o circuit breaker foi acionado duas vezes no mesmo dia. A primeira interrupção ocorreu após uma queda de 10% do Ibovespa. Depois da retomada das negociações, o índice chegou a recuar 15%, provocando uma segunda paralisação.

16 de março : a Bolsa voltou a interromper as operações após o Ibovespa registrar uma queda superior a 12% na abertura do pregão.

18 de março : o mecanismo foi acionado pela sexta e última vez em 2020. Naquele dia, o Ibovespa encerrou o pregão com queda de 10,35%.

Apesar dos seis acionamentos registrados em um único mês de 2020, esse período representa apenas uma pequena parcela de todas as vezes em que o circuit breaker foi acionado na Bolsa brasileira.

Quedas da bolsa em dia de Circuit Breaker — Foto: Arte/g1

Três anos antes da pandemia da covid-19, em 18 de maio de 2017, ocorreu o episódio que ficou conhecido como "Joesley Day", em referência ao empresário Joesley Batista, um dos donos da JBS.

Na véspera, o jornal O Globo havia revelado a existência de uma gravação feita pelo empresário durante uma conversa com o então presidente Michel Temer (MDB). O conteúdo levantou suspeitas de que Temer teria dado aval à compra do silêncio do ex-presidente da Câmara dos Deputados Eduardo Cunha, que estava preso. Temer negou as acusações.

A revelação provocou uma crise política e uma forte reação do mercado financeiro. Na manhã seguinte, o Ibovespa chegou a despencar mais de 10%, acionando o circuit breaker e suspendendo as negociações por 30 minutos. Ao final do pregão, a Bolsa acumulou queda de 8,8%.

Em 2008, durante a crise financeira internacional, o mecanismo também foi acionado diversas vezes. Em 22 de outubro, a bolsa fechou com queda de 10,18%. Naquele mês, as negociações foram interrompidas quatro vezes por 30 minutos e uma vez por uma hora.

Os mercados internacionais enfrentavam forte turbulência diante da quebra de instituições financeiras nos Estados Unidos, da necessidade de socorro bilionário aos bancos e das preocupações com a situação do sistema bancário europeu.

29 de setembro : primeiro acionamento do ano.

6 de outubro : dois acionamentos no mesmo dia.

1999: crise cambial e adoção do câmbio flutuante

Em janeiro de 1999, o circuit breaker também foi acionado na Bolsa brasileira, em meio a uma crise cambial. Na época, o Brasil enfrentava uma intensa saída de dólares do país , enquanto investidores temiam que o governo não conseguisse manter a política de controle da cotação da moeda americana.

A turbulência ganhou força após o Banco Central anunciar mudanças na política cambial. Em 14 de janeiro, as negociações na Bolsa foram suspensas por 30 minutos, após uma queda acentuada das ações. Ao final do pregão, o índice acumulou perdas de 9,33%.

Em 1998, o circuit breaker foi acionado cinco vezes na Bolsa brasileira, em meio à crise financeira que atingiu a Rússia. Naquele ano, o governo russo enfrentava uma grave crise econômica, marcada pela desvalorização de sua moeda e pela dificuldade de pagar suas dívidas, levando investidores a retirar recursos de países considerados mais arriscados, como o Brasil.

Um dos momentos mais críticos ocorreu em 10 de setembro de 1998, quando as negociações na Bolsa brasileira foram interrompidas por uma hora. Ao final daquele pregão, o índice acumulou queda de 15,82%.

A criação do mecanismo e primeiro acionamento

O circuit breaker foi acionado pela primeira vez no Brasil em 28 de outubro de 1997 , em meio à crise financeira asiática, que começou na Tailândia e se espalhou por outros países da região, provocando fortes quedas nas bolsas de valores ao redor do mundo.

Na véspera, a Bolsa de Valores de São Paulo (Bovespa) havia registrado uma queda superior a 14%, pressionada pelo temor dos investidores de que a crise atingisse outras economias. No dia seguinte, o mecanismo foi utilizado pela primeira vez para interromper as negociações e conter o pânico no mercado financeiro. Ainda em 1997, o circuit breaker voltou a ser acionado outras duas vezes.

articles.title: Taubaté lança programa de anistia com descontos de até 100% de juros e multas | G1
articles.standfirst: Programa permite regularizar débitos municipais vencidos até dezembro de 2025, com descontos de até 100% em juros e multas e opções de parcelamento em até 36 vezes.
articles.summary: Programa permite regularizar débitos municipais vencidos até dezembro de 2025, com descontos de até 100% em juros e multas e opções de parcelamento em até 36 vezes.
articles.body:
A Prefeitura de Taubaté instituiu o Programa de Recuperação de Créditos Municipais, ação de anistia de juros e multas destinado à regularização de débitos tributários e não tributários - IPTU, ISS, ITBI, Simube e outros - vencidos até 31 de dezembro de 2025.

Os descontos chegam a 100% sobre multas e juros para pagamentos à vista até 19 de novembro de 2026 e de 90% sobre multas e juros para quitação até 18 de dezembro.

Para o contribuinte que optar pelo parcelamento, os descontos vão até 75%:

6 parcelas: 75% de desconto em juros e multas

12 parcelas: 70% de desconto em juros e multas

24 parcelas: 60% de desconto em juros e multas

36 parcelas: 50% de desconto em juros e multas

O programa terá validade até 18 de dezembro de 2026.

Ficam excluídas do programa as multas administrativas e fiscais, como as decorrentes de infrações de trânsito, penalidades aplicadas pela Vigilância Sanitária, autos de infração urbanística e multas tributárias de caráter punitivo. Também não se enquadram na proposta as restituições ao erário, exceto as referentes à Bolsa Simube.

Além disso, o benefício não abrange condenações pecuniárias resultantes de decisões dos Tribunais de Contas da União e do Estado, nem valores relacionados a ações judiciais de improbidade administrativa, ações populares ou outras decisões semelhantes.

Os contribuintes que desejarem aderir ao programa podem realizar todo o processo de forma online, por meio do portal oficial da Prefeitura de Taubaté ( A medida visa facilitar o acesso dos contribuintes ao programa, garantindo mais agilidade e comodidade no processo de regularização de débitos municipais.

Para atendimento presencial, é necessário fazer o agendamento prévio pelo site da prefeitura ( e comparecer no prédio do Tesourinho (Rua Carneiro de Souza, 99, no centro) no dia e horário marcados.

No atendimento, é necessário apresentar documentação específica: cartão do CNPJ para pessoas jurídicas; RG e CPF para pessoas físicas; número da inscrição cadastral do imóvel ou municipal, conforme o tipo de débito; além de procuração simples no caso de representação por terceiros.

Nos casos de imóveis pertencentes a espólio, devem ser apresentados também a cópia do inventário ou a certidão de óbito do titular.

articles.title: The markets are starting to act seriously weird. Blame AI
articles.summary: AI’s shaky balance sheets raise questions about circular financing that investors have long questioned but the industry and many traders have swept under the...
articles.body:
On the surface, the markets seem stable. Stocks are near record highs, and bonds are right about where they've been for the past couple of months.

But check under the hood, and you'll see signs that investors are growing increasingly nervous — mostly because of AI.

This time, the anxiety isn't because AI is going to kill us all (that was SO last month). The latest concern: AI may be a financial quagmire.

And if the air is starting to come out of the AI bubble, it could threaten to knock over the foundation supporting America's economic boom.

The stock market is so big and diverse that it's sometimes useful for investors to measure it in creative ways, comparing two measurements to figure out if there's a trend that the headline numbers can't show you.

For example, you can measure the benchmark S&P 500 stock index in a number of ways. The most common way is to weight each stock by its market value — giving gigantic tech companies worth trillions of dollars considerable influence over the ups and downs of the stock market.

But if you look at the S&P 500 another way, weighting each stock equally, you can sometimes get a clearer picture of how the market is performing across industries. Equally weighting stocks ensures companies in smaller industries aren't drowned out by massive ones, like Big Tech.

When comparing those two measurements on October 22, the result was seriously bizarre — so strange it had only happened twice before in the past three decades.

The main index, weighted by market value, fell 1.2%. But the equal-weighted index gained 0.5%. Since 1995, that massive divergence in the two measurements had happened only twice before: April 14, 1999, and March 30, 2000, noted James Reilly, senior markets economist at Capital Economics.

What does it mean? A clue can be found in another weird thing that happened that same day.

Also on Thursday, the 10-year Treasury yield slammed on the brakes and went into reverse, falling below 5% and tumbling in the largest single-day decline since March 10, 2023 — the day that Silicon Valley Bank imploded.

So investors were pouring money out of tech and into Treasuries and non-tech stocks at a historic pace.

It's a sign that AI is making some folks on Wall Street kind of nervous.

Bonds had been tumbling (and yields, as a result, had been surging to multi-decade highs) for three core reasons:

The Iran war sent inflation on a serious rebound, cutting off the world's oil and fuel supplies and sending prices through the roof. Bond investors, when confronted with rebounding inflation, demanded higher yields to compensate for the chunk of their investment that inflation has been eating into.

articles.title: Bank of Maharashtra net profits jump 41% to Rs 2309 cr in Q2FY27
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Bank of Maharashtra reported a 41.4 percent year-on-year rise in net profit to Rs 2,309.59 crore in the Sept quarter, driven by higher interest
articles.body: MUMBAI: Bank of Maharashtra reported a 41.4 percent year-on-year rise in net profit to Rs 2,309.59 crore in the Sept quarter, driven by higher interest and non-interest income, improved operating efficiency and lower provisions for bad loans.Net interest income (NII) rose 21.8 percent to Rs 3,954.23 crore. Interest income increased 20.7 percent to Rs 8,606.37 crore while interest expenditure grew 19.9 percent to Rs 4,652.14 crore. The bank's current and savings account (CASA) deposits accounted for more than 50 percent of its deposit base, helping contain funding costs.Other income rose 33.6 percent to Rs 1,129.04 crore. Retail banking contributed Rs 4,374.70 crore to revenue, corporate and wholesale banking Rs 3,543.33 crore, and treasury Rs 1,713.68 crore. Total income, including interest and other income, increased 22.1 percent to Rs 9,735.41 crore.Operating profit rose 30.9 percent to Rs 3,368.67 crore as operating expenses grew 12.9 percent to Rs 1,714.60 crore. Employee costs increased 11.7 percent to Rs 917.88 crore, while other expenses rose 14.4 percent to Rs 796.72 crore. The operating margin stood at 34.6 percent.Provisions and contingencies fell 13.4 percent to Rs 654.45 crore. Provisions for non-performing assets dropped 79.2 percent to Rs 121.11 crore from Rs 583.01 crore a year earlier. Profit before tax rose 49.3 percent to Rs 2,714.22 crore, while tax expense increased to Rs 404.63 crore from Rs 185.24 crore.Gross advances grew around 17 percent year on year to more than Rs 2.54 lakh crore, while deposits rose around 12 percent to over Rs 3.09 lakh crore. The gross non-performing asset ratio improved to 1.25 percent from 1.72 percent, with gross bad loans at Rs 4,113.55 crore. The net NPA ratio declined to 0.12 percent from 0.18 percent, while net bad loans stood at Rs 396.13 crore.The bank's Basel III capital adequacy ratio stood at 18.51 percent, including a common equity tier-1 ratio of 15.61 percent. articles.title: Trump said China was headed for ‘big trouble.’ Yet its economy is growing faster than the U.S., and its deficits are moving in the right direction
articles.summary: Goldman Sachs’ Hui Shan noted over the weekend that China’s Q3 real GDP grew 4.5% year on year, slightly above the consensus expectation of 4.4%.
articles.body:
When President Trump announced his tariff plan 18 months ago, he made it clear who he hoped would pay for the sharp end of the scheme: It wouldn't be U.S. consumers; it would be foreign exporters who would "eat" the increased costs. Indeed, following the tit-for-tat trade war between the U.S. and fellow economic superpower, China, President Trump warned the rival force was headed for "big trouble" if it didn't engage in a "two-way street" of trade. Yet while 100% of U.S. exports to China are reportedly subject to tariffs—and a respective 88.8% of Chinese exports are subject to U.S. tariffs—the world's second-largest economy has continued to grow ahead of expectations, and has seemingly grown its export business with the rest of the world. Goldman Sachs' Hui Shan noted over the weekend that China's Q3 real GDP grew 4.5% year on year, slightly above the consensus expectation of 4.4%. Shan added that September activity data were firmer than expected, with industrial production growth accelerating to 5.5% on a year-on-year basis, and retail sales above expectations.

The growth target of 4.5% to 5% appears on track, noted Shan.

Those are the sort of numbers that growth agenda economists in the U.S. can only dream of—especially when policymakers are advocating a plan to grow the economy out of any fiscal unease owing to the nation's $40 trillion national debt burden. U.S. GDP for the first and second quarters came in at 2.5% and 2.2%, respectively, per the Bureau of Economic Analysis .

That said, data analysts highlight that while the headline figures between the U.S. and China leave something to be desired on the Western side, the U.S. remains the largest economy in the world and has a GDP per capita that dwarfs China's. The International Monetary Fund (IMF) reports China's GDP per capita is $15,370, while that of the U.S. is in excess of $95,000.

On deficits, China also appears to be making some moves in the right direction—though from a more unbalanced starting point. Shan notes: "Contrary to our expectation of moderate fiscal loosening at the beginning of the year, fiscal data have shown effective tightening. In the first nine months of this year, combined revenues from the general public budget and government managed funds increased by 1.4% yoy [year over year], whereas expenditures fell by 3.5% yoy.

"Our estimated augmented fiscal deficit (AFD) narrowed from 11% of GDP in December 2025 to 9.4% in September 2026 on a 12-month moving average basis."

Unlike the U.S., China seems to be reducing its budget deficit as a share of GDP. However, while U.S. policymakers have yet to agree on targets to reduce deficits as a share of GDP, they are already operating from a smaller basis: The Congressional Budget Office's long-term budget projections show total deficits averaging 7.2% of GDP over the next three decades (2026–56).

articles.title: Gasoline Prices Under Trump Surpass Biden-Era Average
articles.summary: The average price Americans are paying for gasoline under President Donald Trump has overtaken the average during the Biden administration, underscoring the...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- The average price Americans are paying for gasoline under President Donald Trump has overtaken the average during the Biden administration, underscoring the political pressure on Republicans ahead of the midterm elections.

Trump had pledged to lower gasoline prices to below $2 a gallon, but almost two years into his presidency the fuel's retail cost has averaged $3.472 a gallon, according to the American Automobile Association. That surpassed the average under former President Joe Biden of $3.471 a gallon by less than a cent, according to daily AAA data released Monday.

Gasoline prices surged this year after the start of the US and Israel's war in Iran, crippling oil flows and further squeezing global refining capacity. Over the past eight months, US average pump prices have risen over $1 a gallon while diesel prices have surged almost $3 a gallon and topped the highest level on record.

Americans have never paid this much for fuel this late in the year, with a national average price of $4.286 a gallon as of Sunday, according to AAA. Biden still holds the record for the single-highest nationwide gasoline price of $5.02 a gallon in June 2022, in the months after Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

The global market is missing around 400,000 barrels a day of gasoline that would normally be exported from the Middle East, said Susan Bell, senior vice president, downstream at Rystad Energy.

The cost of diesel has been the main focus for the Trump administration in the weeks leading up to the midterm elections with prices reaching a record high of $6.53 a gallon last month. Surging fuel prices have vexed inflation-weary voters and are proving to be a sticking point for Trump's Republican party.

Average prices of diesel under Trump has already exceed the same figure under Biden by about 6%. Trump invoked war-time powers on Thursday to boost fuel production in the US, with the Department of Energy announcing Friday that it has $150 million earmarked for investments in refineries.

articles.title: Tesla stock jumps as Barclays bets a SpaceX takeout bump is coming
articles.summary: Barclays believes a Tesla merger with SpaceX will hand shareholders a takeout premium, while the EV maker's core business and robotaxi push gain momentum.
articles.body:
Barclays believes a Tesla ( TSLA ) merger with SpaceX ( SPCX ) will deliver a takeout premium to shareholders while the EV maker's core business and robotaxi push gain momentum.

Lead analyst Dan Levy upgraded Tesla to Overweight from Equal Weight, and raised his price target to $450 from $370, citing the confluence of positive factors.

"We believe the improvement in Tesla's core business + inflection in Robotaxi, alongside the potential premium from a combination with SPCX [SpaceX], offers attractive risk/reward for the stock," Levy wrote.

On SpaceX's earnings call last week, CEO Elon Musk disclosed that both companies had formed special committees to discuss a deal. He said there was "a lot of merit to combining the companies."

Musk has long said he wants around 25% of Tesla, versus 20% today. He owns about 48% of SpaceX and holds around 82% of its voting power through super-voting Class B shares.

Levy called "Musk's desire to consolidate control" the "crucial element."

Barclays sees an all-stock acquisition of Tesla by SpaceX as the most likely structure. At $450 a share, or a 20% premium, SpaceX would need to offer around 3.1 of its stock per Tesla share. That would leave Musk with about 53% of the combined company's voting power.

Approval requires more than 50% of total outstanding shares, and abstentions count as "no" votes. "While we expect a merger vote would still pass, we do not see it as a surefire approval," Levy wrote. Barclays' $250 downside case assumes no deal happens.

Beyond the deal, Levy sees improving fundamentals. Tesla is on track to grow deliveries this year after two straight annual declines. Barclays forecasts 1.80 million vehicles in 2026 and 1.92 million in 2027.

Full self-driving (FSD) was on more than 75% of North American deliveries in the third quarter , up about 20 percentage points from the second quarter. Exports from Giga Shanghai now make up around 25%-30% of global volume.

Energy is another bright spot. Management said Tesla is nearly sold out of megapacks for 2027 on strong data center demand. Barclays sees deployments growing at least 50% next year as Megafactory Houston ramps up.

As of Oct. 18, Tesla's robotaxi fleet had logged around 3.1 million unsupervised miles across 6 cities, up from about 400,000 in mid-July. Weekly miles jumped from 70,000 to around 560,000 over that span.

Barclays doesn't expect robotaxis to matter financially in the near- to mid-term. But it argues "signs of significant progress in its operational cities could drive the narrative on the stock."

Pras Subramanian is Lead Auto Reporter for Yahoo Finance. You can follow him on X and on Instagram .

articles.title: Merck Drug Boosts Survival From Hard-to-Treat Uterine Cancer
articles.summary: An experimental drug from Merck & Co. helped women with advanced endometrial cancer live significantly longer than those receiving chemotherapy, bolstering t...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- An experimental drug from Merck & Co. helped women with advanced endometrial cancer live significantly longer than those receiving chemotherapy, bolstering the company's ambitions for the novel treatment it is studying in a wide range of tumors.

Patients receiving sacituzumab tirumotecan, known as sac-TMT, lived a median of 19 months, compared with 12.1 months for those given chemotherapy, according to results from a late-stage study presented at the European Society for Medical Oncology congress on Monday. The treatment also came with significant side effects, including anemia and debilitating mouth sores.

Merck previously said the trial met its goals, without providing details. The full results show the extent of the benefit for patients, who typically die within a year if their disease progresses after chemotherapy. About 68,000 US women are expected to be diagnosed with uterine cancer in 2026, according to the American Cancer Society.

"It is one of the only cancers with an increasing rate of mortality," Dean Li, president of Merck Research Laboratories, said in an interview before the data were released. "What we're trying to do is shift that."

The findings could pave the way for sac-TMT's first US approval, an important milestone for the drug being tested in 17 late-stage studies across numerous types of cancer. Merck acquired rights to the treatment outside China through a deal with Sichuan Kelun-Biotech Biopharmaceutical Co., betting it could become a major addition to its oncology business as its blockbuster drug Keytruda faces looming competition from cheaper copies.

But the bigger prize remains ahead. Merck is pursuing sac-TMT in lung cancer and other common tumors, where successful trials could open up substantially larger commercial opportunities. Analysts at HSBC estimate that sac-TMT and its combinations could be a $12 billion to $15 billion opportunity.

Much of that enthusiasm has centered on non-small cell lung cancer. Lung cancer is the most common tumor type in the world, and non-small cell is by far the most prevalent type.

Over the weekend, Merck shared results from a study in China, where sac-TMT combined with Keytruda reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 51% compared with standard treatment. The results, published in the New England Journal of Medicine, exceeded Wall Street's expectations and bolstered confidence in the drug's potential, analysts from RBC Capital Markets said in a note.

articles.title: Microsoft offers voluntary buyout to 60,000 employees
articles.summary: Microsoft (MSFT) announced it was offering voluntary buyouts to roughly 60,000 employees on Monday as it looks to reshape its organization for the AI era.
articles.body:
Microsoft ( MSFT ) announced on Monday that it was offering voluntary buyouts to roughly 60,000 employees as it looks to reshape its organization for the AI era.

"The Voluntary Exit Offer reflects an important part of how we're evolving our approach to change: creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter," Amy Coleman, Microsoft's executive vice president and chief people officer, wrote in a memo to employees.

The company is reportedly offering buyouts to employees in Canada, India, the United Kingdom, and the United States at level 70 and below, which includes some senior-level personnel.

The announcement follows Microsoft's first voluntary retirement program , which it announced in May. The retirement packages offered ranged from eight to 39 weeks of base pay, depending on employees' positions and tenure.

The offers to staff come as Microsoft plans to spend $190 billion on capital expenditures in 2026, largely tied to its investments in artificial intelligence.

All eyes will be on the Big Tech giant on Wednesday, when Microsoft releases its quarterly earnings and provides an update on its capex plans and Azure cloud growth.

articles.title: Elon Musk vows to give every US child SpaceX stock
articles.summary: Elon Musk says he'll give one SpaceX share to every kid in America in 2027, but key details about eligibility and distribution remain unclear.
articles.body: You probably don't expect Elon Musk to show up in your child's investment portfolio. But that's exactly what could happen next year. The billionaire behind SpaceX has made a remarkable promise. He says he'll give one share of his space company to every kid in America. We're talking about a potential giveaway worth more than $10 billion. Free SpaceX stock for kids sounds appealing, especially when you're thinking about your child's financial future. But before you start looking for a way to sign up, there are some pretty important details Musk has yet to explain. Join our upcoming CyberGuy LIVE class: 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money In this free live online class, Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will share five practical ways to protect your trip and your wallet this holiday travel season. You’ll learn how to secure your phone and personal information, find better travel deals, avoid common scams, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed. Join us Saturday, October 31, at 11 AM ET / 8 AM PT. Register free now at CyberGuyLive.com. NEW BOOK ON ELON MUSK EXAMINES THE BILLIONAIRE’S MIND, MOTIVATION AND MAKING LIFE MULTI-PLANETARY Elon Musk promises SpaceX shares to every US child Musk recently announced on X that he plans to give one of his SpaceX shares to every kid in America in 2027. "Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America. This will be the first of many," Musk wrote. That's a sweeping commitment. SpaceX, which went public in June 2026, operates the Starlink satellite internet network and develops rockets for commercial spaceflight. Now Musk wants millions of American children to own a tiny piece of the company. The promise has already attracted attention because of its enormous potential cost. However, Musk hasn't provided a detailed plan explaining how the shares would reach families or which children would qualify. How much would the SpaceX shares be worth? For perspective, SpaceX shares closed at $147.49 on Oct. 23. There are just over 72 million Americans under age 18. Using that closing price, giving every one of them a share would cost approximately $10.6 billion. For a family with two eligible children, that could mean roughly $295 worth of SpaceX stock based on the Oct. 23 valuation. Of course, that amount could change considerably by 2027. Stock prices rise and fall, and owning a single share offers no guarantee of future profits. Still, there's something intriguing about the idea of a child becoming an investor before graduating from high school. If SpaceX continues to grow, that share could become more valuable over time. On the other hand, families could also watch its value decline. Why Musk's SpaceX promise followed Anthropic's announcement The timing is especially interesting. Just one day before Musk made his announcement, artificial intelligence company Anthropic revealed a major philanthropic commitment of its own. The company behind Claude AI announced plans to commit 5% of its shares to a new Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, subject to stockholder approval. The fund could support nonprofit organizations or provide direct financial assistance to certain populations, including workers affected by AI-driven economic changes. The company also described a structure that could increase its contribution as its valuation grows, subject to future board decisions. Musk responded to Anthropic's announcement by recommending that companies give shares directly to the public. He then followed up with his own pledge involving SpaceX. This exchange raises an interesting question about the enormous wealth accumulating around AI. As technology companies become increasingly valuable, executives are facing greater scrutiny over how that wealth should benefit the public. SEN DAVE MCCORMICK: TRUMP ACCOUNTS GIVE ALL AMERICANS A STAKE IN PROSPERITY Could SpaceX shares be connected to Trump Accounts? Under the Trump Accounts program, the Treasury Department began automatically enrolling eligible children in tax-advantaged investment accounts on Oct. 1. Parents or guardians must still claim and activate those accounts before managing them. A separate federal pilot program provides a one-time $1,000 contribution for qualifying U.S. citizen children born between Jan. 1, 2025 and Dec. 31, 2028. Families must make an election to receive that contribution. SpaceX President and Chief Operating Officer Gwynne Shotwell and her husband, Robert Shotwell, previously pledged to donate one SpaceX share to the Trump Account of each of more than 2 million children. Their contribution targets children ages 11 to 17 in areas with lower-than-average household incomes, with additional emphasis on communities near their home in central Texas. New Treasury regulations that took effect Sept. 30 also allow qualifying donations of publicly traded company shares into Trump Accounts. Under those rules, donated shares generally must be held for five years or until the account's special growth period ends, whichever comes first. Musk's proposal could potentially use this system, but he has not publicly explained the exact distribution process. That's an important unanswered question because Trump Accounts have established eligibility requirements and investment rules. Musk's announcement appears to cover a much broader population of children, although he has yet to define exactly who qualifies. What questions remain about Musk's SpaceX giveaway? A pledge this large naturally comes with logistical challenges. For starters, Musk hasn't clarified whether every child under 18 would qualify or whether the giveaway would be limited to U.S. citizens. It is also unclear how children would receive their shares. If the giveaway uses Trump Accounts, families would need to understand how eligibility and account requirements apply. If Musk chooses another distribution method, parents may need some type of custodial account to hold stock for a minor. But Musk has not identified a specific process for families to claim his promised shares. There are also financial questions. Would families face any tax consequences? Could children sell their shares immediately, or would restrictions apply? And when during 2027 would the transfers happen? For now, there's no confirmed application process for Musk's nationwide pledge. Parents should be cautious of anyone claiming otherwise. UKRAINE'S STARLINK RESTORED AS ELON MUSK CLAIMS KYIV VIOLATED TERMS OF SERVICE 'TO KILL PEOPLE' What this means to you If you have children or grandchildren, this is certainly a development worth following. A free share of SpaceX could introduce young people to investing and give them a financial interest in a company developing space technology. But I'd encourage parents to be patient. Musk has not announced an official enrollment process for his proposed giveaway. That means you should be especially suspicious of websites or social media messages claiming you can already register your children for free SpaceX stock. We have previously reported on scams using Elon Musk's name to promote questionable products. A high-profile stock giveaway could provide another opportunity for impersonators to target families. Avoid sharing your child's Social Security number, financial information or other sensitive details with anyone promoting an unverified giveaway. For legitimate information about Trump Accounts, visit the IRS website at irs.gov/trumpaccounts directly. That official program already has an established enrollment process, but signing up for a Trump Account does not guarantee your child will receive a share from Musk's pledge. If SpaceX eventually announces a formal process, review the eligibility requirements and any account restrictions before participating. Kurt's key takeaways I've seen Elon Musk make some pretty ambitious promises over the years, but offering a piece of SpaceX to every child in America is certainly an attention-grabber. What interests me most is the idea of giving young people an ownership stake in a company helping shape the future of space exploration. There could be real financial value in that over time. Still, I want to see the details before getting too excited. A promise involving billions of dollars and millions of children deserves a clear explanation of how it will work. I also find the timing fascinating. With Anthropic making its own massive commitment to public benefit, we're beginning to see tech billionaires debate who should share in the wealth their companies create. I'll be watching to see whether Musk follows through and how much of that wealth actually reaches American families. articles.title: ‘Everything destroyed’: Hebron businesses count cost of Israeli assault
articles.summary: Israeli demolitions and road closures have devastated businesses in Hebron, leaving owners facing millions in losses.
articles.body:
Hebron, occupied West Bank – Sufyan al-Qawasmi stood near the rubble of his factories in the Farsh al-Hawa area of Hebron, lamenting the business he watched vanish beneath the debris.

Israeli bulldozers demolished the factories on Friday without any prior warning or notice, following a shooting attack carried out by two Palestinians that morning near Hebron’s western entrance. The attack killed two Israeli soldiers , as well as the two Palestinian gunmen, and prompted Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to announce a large-scale military operation across Hebron and order preparations for a wider closure of the illegally occupied West Bank.

Demolitions are regularly used by Israel to punish Palestinians, typically the family members of attackers, but in al-Qawasmi’s case, for the misfortune of being close to the site of an attack. Human rights groups decry the practice, which is regarded as collective punishment.

Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich justified the demolitions as “establishing deterrence and exacting a price”.

The Israeli bulldozers destroyed a business that al-Qawasmi’s family had built up for his whole life, and provided a livelihood for more than 70 people. The first factory, which produced ceramics, is the same age as he is – it was established 50 years ago. Fifteen years later, the family opened a marble factory.

Their business flourished, becoming one of the most significant industrial operations in the West Bank, with goods exported to Israel.

In the space of a few hours on Friday, the ceramic factory and marble factory were gone, as well as several neighbouring buildings, including a three-storey house and various commercial facilities. Simultaneously, the city faced an Israeli military incursion that included the closure of all entrances, raids, arrests, and the forced evacuation of more than 3,000 Palestinians from their homes, severely disrupting the lives of residents and the city’s commercial activity.

The message was clear: the whole city would be punished for the actions of the attackers.

Al-Qawasmi says he was given no chance to retrieve goods from the family businesses’ warehouses and factories before the demolitions began, leaving the stock buried under the rubble, where it remains.

“We managed to retrieve some marble slabs and store them in facilities belonging to friends nearby, but most of the stock was destroyed,” he told Al Jazeera.

Al-Qawasmi says that 1,300 square metres of their business’ property was destroyed, including the family’s offices. He estimates the losses at no less than 60 million shekels ($19m).

Those losses are devastating for al-Qawasmi’s family, but also for the wider economy in Hebron and the Palestinian economy as a whole.

According to the Hebron Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Hebron serves as a primary pillar of the Palestinian economy, contributing approximately 42 percent of the Palestinian gross domestic product (GDP). It is home to more than 23,000 economic establishments, including more than 5,000 industrial and artisanal facilities that employ approximately 40,000 workers.

Hebron’s economy is notably diverse, encompassing sectors such as stone and marble, plastics, metals, food production, leather and footwear, and glass, alongside robust commercial and agricultural activity.

Adnan al-Natsha, vice president of the Hebron Chamber of Commerce, told Al Jazeera that there are no precise figures yet regarding the total losses resulting from the Israeli military operation so far. He noted that work is currently under way to compile statistics on the damage inflicted on businesses and homes, losses estimated to be in the millions of dollars.

Al-Natsha explained that the extensive Israeli measures, including closing off areas of the city, displacing residents from their homes, demolishing buildings and shutting down commercial shops, have exacerbated the already difficult economic situation in Hebron – which already has an illegal Israeli settlement in its commercial centre that severely disrupts Palestinian movement and trade there.

“Business owners have been unable to operate their facilities because workers couldn’t reach their workplaces, and employees have been unable to get to their jobs. The impact of these measures is not limited to Hebron; it extends to the Palestinian economy as a whole,” he stated, adding that work was ongoing to assess the losses and damages of the ongoing Israeli operation so far.

The Israeli military continues to lock down Hebron, including the installation of checkpoints, earthen berms, and concrete blocks across the city, as it conducts raids. As a consequence, economic activity has been severely disrupted.

Ibrahim Ahmaro, who owns a vegetable shop in the al-Jalada neighbourhood, one of the areas targeted by the Israeli operation, told Al Jazeera that he had been arranging his stock on Friday, preparing for Saturday, which is typically the busiest day for commerce due to the arrival of buses carrying Palestinian citizens of Israel shopping for cheaper produce.

Military vehicles suddenly stormed the area, and soldiers forced Ahmaro to leave his shop immediately. He says that he wasn’t given an opportunity to turn on the refrigeration units, which would have kept his goods from spoiling, nor allowed to retrieve his vehicle, which remained parked in front of the shop.

“My brother, the staff and I all left, thinking it would only be for a few hours. Instead, we were met with a total lockdown of the area, and we were unable to reach our shops, meaning everything inside was lost after being left unattended for days,” he added.

On Sunday morning, Ahmaro was able to return to check on his stock, despite the heavy military presence in the area. As soon as he entered, he said soldiers attacked him inside the shop and forced him out. He pleaded with them to let him remove at least a few crates; they granted him a few minutes to do so.

“I placed the crates 400 metres away from the shops so that local residents, facing the lockdown, could take whatever they needed. My losses on these goods alone exceed 50,000 shekels [$16,200],” he said with a sigh.

Economic expert Ali Oweiwi said that the Israeli military’s restrictions and lockdowns imposed on Hebron have created significant challenges for commercial and industrial establishments, which rely on road access to transport production supplies and distribute their products.

He explained that the impact of the closure is not limited to retail shops but extends to companies, factories, suppliers, and the transport and logistics sector, not to mention the workers who are forced to take alternative routes to reach their workplaces, all of which ultimately affect consumers.

Oweiwi said that if the Israeli operation concludes within a day or two, the economy might recover relatively quickly. However, if it persists for more than 10 days, it could lead to significant problems, including the accumulation of goods, disruptions to transport and a decline in productivity due to the difficulty of moving both workers and merchandise.

Israel – which will vote for a new parliament in pivotal elections on Tuesday – has not announced an end date for the lockdown in Hebron.

“The destruction of facilities specialising in vehicle dismantling, spare parts, and tile shops has resulted in losses estimated at 70 to 80 million shekels ($22.7m to $26m), in addition to the seizure of dozens or perhaps hundreds of vehicles belonging to the owners of these establishments,” Oweiwi said.

articles.title: Unleash the Export-Import Bank to outcompete China
articles.summary: Sen. Kevin Cramer is calling on Congress to reauthorize and modernize the Export-Import Bank by Dec. 31 to prevent China from dominating global energy markets and to protect over 45,000 U.S. jobs.
articles.body:
Congress faces a stark choice this year: strengthen America’s ability to compete abroad or let China dominate global markets. At the end of this year, the charter of the Export-Import Bank of the United States (known widely as EXIM) expires , stranding over $70 billion in projects sitting in its deal pipeline. These projects include important strategic energy and critical minerals projects, and would support over 45,000 U.S. jobs. Congress must act by Dec. 31 to keep these projects on track or U.S. workers will pay the price and America’s competitors will fill the gap.

Reauthorizing and modernizing EXIM will supercharge one of America’s most powerful tools to strengthen U.S. economic competitiveness and energy leadership at a time when aggressive, pro-energy development is needed on the global stage — and is being provided by our greatest adversary.

Since 2015, Beijing has poured at least $446 billion into global energy infrastructure and exports , nearly 10 times what the United States has invested. Chinese energy technologies aren’t being built because they are better, they’re being built because China’s state banks arrive with heavy subsidies and predatory loans.

Our strategy should be uniquely American to beat this kind of state-directed competition. EXIM operates at no cost to American taxpayers . It doesn’t crowd out private capital — it steps in where private lenders won’t go alone or when foreign governments have already put a thumb on the scale. We should use EXIM as a key to unlock global sales. Leveraging our dynamic private capital markets through EXIM unleashes American innovators and builders at home, who then export our leadership and sell U.S. energy solutions to the world.

A modern, well-capitalized EXIM will build on American strengths in technologies like nuclear energy, liquefied natural gas and geothermal into signed contracts instead of missed opportunities.

But EXIM competes with one hand tied behind its back; instead of standing alone as an example of American innovation, it stands alone as an example of American bureaucratic excess. Its culture of risk aversion runs deep, resulting in EXIM leaving three-quarters of its lending authority untouched even as our adversaries lean into cutting-edge projects.

EXIM’s recent Competitiveness Report found governments are using export credit at the highest levels seen in a decade and relying on these agencies to win projects in strategic industries. While foreign governments finance aggressively to win global contracts, American exporters are left at a serious disadvantage, which an authorization lapse would exacerbate.

American businesses have paid this price before. When EXIM lost its authorization and board quorum from 2015 to 2019 , American exporters lost business to foreign competitors. A bipartisan, 10 year reauthorization of EXIM, the longest term in the bank’s history, will send a signal to American workers and our global competition Washington’s commitment to invest in the success of American business abroad.

To arm EXIM with a genuine competitive edge and foster the export of innovative technologies, it needs a modernized approach to risk management and project selection. In June, EXIM’s advisory committee, an expert panel of external industry, finance and labor leaders, recommended eliminating the existing 2 percent default rate shutdown trigger and implementing bolder risk standards. These modernizations will allow the bank to back transactions that advance American national and economic interests while upholding EXIM’s strong financial track record.

American companies are building the energy technologies the world wants to buy. The country financing the next decade’s energy infrastructure and critical minerals supply chains will set the terms of engagement this century and determine if they will be rooted in peace, prosperity and power or heavy-handed government oppression. Congress must reauthorize the Export-Import Bank for the long haul, equip it to compete, then let American innovators, workers and technology do the rest. The alternative is watching China power the next decade on its own terms.

Kevin Cramer is North Dakota’s junior U.S. senator and a member of the Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee.

articles.title: Anthropic’s IPO filing shows explosive growth, risks and staggering costs
articles.summary: The filing sets up the company for a Wall Street debut next month, potentially eclipsing SpaceX’s IPO.
articles.body:
Artificial intelligence giant Anthropic has filed papers for what could be the biggest ever initial public offering (IPO) of stock, even as its top executive warns that advanced AI could pose an existential threat to humanity.

The filing on Monday sets up the San Francisco company for a Wall Street debut next month, potentially eclipsing the SpaceX initial public offering in June that raised a record $86bn.

The filing comes weeks after chief executive and cofounder Dario Amodei argued in an essay for slowing the development of the most advanced AI models. An IPO could provide Anthropic with enormous resources to accelerate its expansion. The amount the company ultimately raises remains uncertain, as does its final valuation and offering price. But even at lower estimates, it would turn the five-year-old startup into one of the world’s most valuable companies and potentially boost the wealth of Amodei and his sister and cofounder, Daniela, by billions of dollars.

The prospectus highlights the AI company’s rapid growth over the past year, fuelled by Big Tech’s breakneck spending that has driven a rally in AI stocks, while raising concerns about lofty valuations and rising debt.

The company also flagged growing risks from AI technology, underscoring concerns over its potential to cause harm, which had led Amodei to call for a slowdown in development of advanced models.

Anthropic’s net loss in the first half of 2026 widened sharply to $80.7bn , largely due to a rise in the fair value of bonds convertible into the company’s shares. Revenue in the period was about $16.3bn.

The company’s revenue grew a staggering 1,368 percent in the three months ended June 30 from a year ago, but warned in the prospectus that the revenue growth rate could decline over time and fluctuate occasionally.

The IPO, which is anticipated to be before Thanksgiving in the US, late next month, is expected to establish Anthropic, the AI lab behind the viral Claude models, as a benchmark for how Wall Street values leading AI companies, including rival OpenAI.

The IPO push comes despite a once-busy autumn listing calendar thinning out as choppy markets prompt companies to delay their offerings. Analysts said that would give Anthropic access to a deep pool of capital to fund its costly AI ambitions.

Growing investor unease with the debt-fuelled AI investment boom has led to a global selloff in AI and tech stocks, as they start to doubt whether the trillions spent on data centres, chips and computing capacity will generate fast returns to support lofty valuations. Higher borrowing costs and rising bond yields have added to their caution.

However, tech companies are still hungry for cash. Meta is aiming to raise up to $95bn in its largest-ever equity fundraising, while SpaceX has inked a $40bn deal with Apollo to lease AI chips and server hardware.

Some current and prospective investors are valuing Anthropic at about $1.5 trillion, down from roughly $2 trillion a week ago, after the AI startup disclosed some financial details at a recent investor event, Reuters reported.

The prospectus also details the risks posed by increasingly powerful AI, from potential misuse and security threats to concerns that advanced systems could produce outputs that “could be interpreted as coercive, deceptive, or manipulative”.

“Anthropic’s IPO will establish a benchmark for valuing leading AI labs, influencing both upcoming listings and confidence in the companies funding the AI infrastructure build-out,” IPOX research associate Lukas Muehlbauer said.

“Its success would not necessarily benefit every AI business equally,” he added.

Anthropic said that more than half of Fortune 500 companies and over 30 percent of Global 2000 firms were customers generating at least $100,000 each in revenue for the company over the 12 months ended September 30.

The IPO comes as Anthropic’s own research raises concerns about advanced AI systems, which in controlled tests have shown behaviours including code sabotage, fraud assistance and information manipulation.

The findings have fuelled concerns about how companies can keep powerful AI systems under control as they race to deploy them commercially.

The ‌‌‌‌prospectus also highlighted risks associated with its AI models, which it said could exhibit “self-preserving behaviours”, including behaviour “resembling blackmail”.

“Our increasing use of AI systems to accelerate our own research and development may cause the capabilities of our models to advance more rapidly than our ability to develop, validate and implement corresponding safety, alignment and security measures,” it said.

The company said it relies on a limited number of cloud service providers, such as Amazon, Google and Microsoft and suppliers such as Broadcom for compute and critical parts of its infrastructure. These relationships can create “dependencies and potential vulnerabilities”, it said.

Anthropic will trade on the Nasdaq after the IPO closes under the ticker symbol “ANT”.

The filing did not reveal the terms of its offering, including the number of shares it plans to sell and the proposed price range.

Anthropic, founded in 2021 by a team of researchers, was valued at $965bn in May in a funding round that drew some of the biggest names in Silicon Valley and Wall Street.

Amazon and Google were among Anthropic’s early strategic partners, investing billions of dollars in the startup while providing the cloud infrastructure needed to train and deploy Claude models.

“We believe this abundance of AI will rapidly transform every sector of the global economy in ways greater than the impact of industrialisation, electricity, semiconductors and the internet,” the prospectus said.

The company said it expects compute and infrastructure expenses to increase in absolute dollars and remain its largest operating expense for the foreseeable future.

Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley were named as the lead banks for the IPO alongside 20 others as underwriters. Morgan Stanley will act as a stabilisation agent, overseeing the stock’s early trading.

The roles mark another major win for Goldman and Morgan Stanley as they also led SpaceX’s IPO.

articles.title: Audi CEO faces backlash after joining Trump at midterm campaign rally
articles.summary: BERLIN, Oct 26 (Reuters) - Audi chief Gernot Doellner drew heavy criticism on Monday for appearing alongside US President Donald Trump at a campaign rally in...
articles.body:
BERLIN, Oct 26 (Reuters) - Audi chief Gernot Doellner drew heavy criticism on Monday for appearing alongside US President Donald Trump at a campaign rally in the battleground state of Georgia, with the head of Germany's top union saying it violated the automaker's company guidelines.

Doellner appeared alongside Trump ‌at the rally in Perry, near Macon in central Georgia, to announce plans to build a $4 billion plant, the luxury carmaker's first in the US, which would ‌produce 200,000 SUVs annually.

TOP VW COMMITTEE MUST DECIDE ON US PLANT

The announcement of the plan, which needs approval by the supervisory board of parent Volkswagen, including German labour representatives, follows lengthy considerations over launching US production to escape import ​tariffs that cost Audi around €1.2 billion ($1.3 billion) last year.

"Doellner is also in flagrant breach of his own company's rules, which expressly require political neutrality in the run-up to elections," said Christiane Benner, head of Germany's IG Metall union and deputy chair of Volkswagen's supervisory board.

The US state of Georgia will support Audi's investment with $1.4 billion, German news outlet Focus reported on Monday, citing a person familiar with the matter.

Audi said a delegation had travelled to Georgia to advance negotiations over the planned plant and accepted an invitation to present the project alongside Trump.

"We accepted this invitation solely with Audi's ‌best interests in mind," the company said in a statement. It ⁠also said it was taking very seriously the notion that Doellner's appearance was being interpreted as a sign of political support.

A person familiar with the matter said Audi's management board had cleared an exception to the company's code of conduct before Doellner's appearance. Under the code, the board ⁠can allow deviations from the rules except in cases involving criminal offences, the source said.

The automaker's top stakeholders discussed the matter during a meeting attended by Benner and another labour representative Daniela Cavallo, with the latter expressing reservations about the appearance without formally opposing it, the person said.

"From a pure business perspective, localising Audi's production in the US may make sense," Cavallo said in comments shared internally and seen ​by ​Reuters. However, with his appearance, Doellner "allowed himself to be turned into a puppet in the propaganda show" of ​Trump, she said.

A second person confirmed that Volkswagen's supervisory board committee — which ‌is already fraught with tension over the company's sweeping restructuring — had discussed the issue on Friday.

articles.title: Apple’s Foldable iPhone Duo Draws Early Complaints of the Screen Cracking
articles.summary: The iPhone Duo, one of Apple Inc.’s biggest new products in years, is drawing a growing number of complaints from customers who say the foldable display crac...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- The iPhone Duo, one of Apple Inc.'s biggest new products in years, is drawing a growing number of complaints from customers who say the foldable display cracked after just hours or days of use.

In these cases, customers reported hearing a crunching sound when unfolding the phone, followed by a large crack forming along the center crease. Some users also experienced a white patch or other display malfunction on the right side of the screen.

Reports of the problem first surfaced on Reddit and other social media sites. Bloomberg News has since independently verified the issue with more than half a dozen customers, who provided photos showing damage to their devices or evidence of their support conversations with Apple.

Apple acknowledged the issue in a statement, saying it was "aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units."

"If users experience issues with their iPhone Duo display, they should contact AppleCare for a replacement," the Cupertino, California-based company said. Most Duos aren't affected by the problem, and the units that are impacted exhibit the defect quickly, Apple said.

"I went to unfold it and it felt stuck/harder/slower to open than usual. And when I opened it it had the lines on the screen," Tom Battle, an Apple customer from San Diego, told Bloomberg. "You could feel a bump or loose piece under the display."

Venture capitalist Jonathan King had a similar experience, saying he heard a crunch-like sound when opening his device on Monday.

"I had all intent to post a positive review of my Duo experience today, until it happened to me," King said. "The smaller outer screen works just fine, but the inner screen is now unusable," he said, adding that the device thinks he is touching the inner screen when he is not.

While the problem appears to affect only a subset of units, it represents an embarrassing setback for Apple, which spent more than a decade developing the device and touted its superior durability, hinge design and display technology.

The Duo, which went on sale Friday, represents the company's first foray into foldable phones — and the biggest-ever design change to the iPhone, Apple's largest source of revenue. Like other foldable phones, the device has a smaller screen on its outer surface and can be opened to reveal a larger display.

articles.title: Pulte vows action against ‘abusive monopolies’ in mortgage market
articles.summary: Bill Pulte, the director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA), said Monday he will not tolerate “abusive monopolies” dominating the mortgage market. “Abusive monopolies will not be allowed to take advantage of consumers anywhere in the mortgage market,” Pulte wrote Monday on social platform X. Pulte said last month that Fannie Mae and Freddie…
articles.body:
Bill Pulte, the director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA), said Monday he will not tolerate “abusive monopolies” dominating the mortgage market .

“Abusive monopolies will not be allowed to take advantage of consumers anywhere in the mortgage market,” Pulte wrote Monday on social platform X .

Pulte said last month that Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac were adopting the VantageScore credit index for mortgage pricing.

An individual’s VantageScore — which was jointly created by credit bureaus Experian, Equifax and TransUnion — is now juxtaposed against their Classic FICO score, the mortgage industry standard for decades.

“We are Simplifying Mortgage Pricing following feedback from lenders and consumers,” Pulte wrote on X in September. “Instead of two separate pricing grids, which makes zero sense, Fannie and Freddie are hereby moving to ONE PRICING GRID with VantageScore joining the existing FICO Classic pricing grid.”

Pulte, whose agency regulates Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, had directed the government-backed enterprises to update their selling guides with the VantageScore and FICO Score 10T indexes in April.

The FHFA director has sought to ease FICO’s grip on the credit score market, as mortgage rates soar above 7 percent.

“Since 2020, FICO has increased the price per a person’s credit score by 1,800%. FICO has enjoyed a monopoly. No more,” he wrote on X in early September.

The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate declined last week, falling from 7.4 percent to 7.32 percent, according to data from Freddie Mac. Mortgage rates have otherwise risen amid higher bond yields and oil prices due to the Iran war.

The Trump administration has taken multiple actions to ease access to homes ahead of the midterms, as Republicans face economic headwinds at the ballot box.

President Trump on Thursday directed Pulte to create a pilot program to cancel insurance premiums for government-backed mortgages once a borrower has satisfied equity requirements.

Also on Thursday, the Treasury Department moved to ban Wall Street investors from purchasing single-family homes — part of a bipartisan housing law Congress passed in June.

articles.title: Anthropic is leasing data centers to reduce reliance on Amazon, Google, others
articles.summary: Anthropic is looking to ease its dependence on third-party cloud providers by entering into its own data center leases.
articles.body:
Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) says it is increasingly leaning into leasing AI data centers to power its vast computing needs.

The company calls the initiative Anthropic Direct and says that it helps address its compute requirements beyond simply leasing capacity from cloud service providers such as Amazon ( AMZN ) and Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ), according to Anthropic's S-1 investor prospectus, which it made public Monday .

"As our compute requirements have scaled, we have transitioned to a hybrid model in which, in addition to purchasing compute as a cloud service, we also procure specialized AI accelerators directly and operate this hardware in dedicated data center facilities leased and operated on our behalf, to our specification," the company says.

The move could also provide long-term economic advantages, according to Anthropic.

In November 2025, the company announced a $50 billion investment that will see Fluidstack build data centers in Texas and New York through which Anthropic will lease computing capacity. The company says it is also directly leasing data center capacity and plans to sign additional agreements going forward.

The moves make Anthropic a major player in the data center space, but also come at a time when the facilities continue to draw backlash from communities across the country over concerns about air and noise pollution and water usage.

Towns and counties throughout the US have issued moratoriums or outright bans on developing data centers in their regions. New York has issued a one-year, statewide moratorium, while Texas has halted data center permitting until it can determine the impact the power-hungry sites will have on its grid.

Anthropic lists the threat of further moratoriums on data centers as a key risk factor for the company in its prospectus.

"Opposition to data center development has also become more organized and coordinated across jurisdictions, and our public profile may draw particular attention to projects associated with us," the company wrote in its S-1.

"The loss of, or a significant disruption at, any major facility may not be readily absorbed by our remaining or future infrastructure. We are expanding our data center capacity internationally as part of our efforts to diversify our infrastructure footprint and reduce concentration risks associated with operating a significant portion of our compute infrastructure in the United States and to support our international growth strategy," Anthropic added.

Data centers have also become a key topic in the 2027 midterms, with voters on both sides of the aisle expressing disapproval.

articles.title: Microsoft offers buyouts to around 60,000 employees to contain costs
articles.summary: Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees as the technology giant looks to contain costs and help fund its massive AI investments.
articles.body: Microsoft said on Monday it is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, or more than a quarter of its global workforce, as the technology giant looks to contain costs and help fund its massive AI investments. Staffers across the Windows maker would be eligible for the offers, including those working in AI experiences, Copilot, finance, human resources, Xbox and Windows + Devices, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters, requesting anonymity as the matter was private. Units such as marketing, commercial business and security will be excluded, the source added. “This offer gives eligible employees who may be considering a future outside the company a new choice to make that transition now with support. It also gives participating organizations another way to adapt their workforce to changing needs,” Chief People Officer Amy Coleman said in a staff memo. Like other tech giants, Microsoft is spending hundreds of billions of dollars on AI data centers and chips, drawing scrutiny from investors over whether the returns will justify the staggering cost. The company, slated to report first-quarter results after markets close on Wednesday, has forecast $175 billion in capital expenditures for the 2026 calendar year. Microsoft had 223,000 full-time employees globally as of June 30, 2026, according to its annual filing. Shares of Microsoft, which had risen about 10% this year, were up about 1% on Monday. The development was first reported by Business Insider. The company earlier this year offered voluntary buyouts to about 7% of its US ​workforce, or about 9,000 employees. In July, Microsoft announced it would cut 4,800 jobs, or ​about 2.1% of its global workforce, overhauling its Xbox gaming business and divesting up to five studios as it looks to ‌boost returns after years of heavy investment in the division. “This offer will be available to eligible employees in participating teams in Canada, India, the United Kingdom and the United States at level 70 and below,” Microsoft said on Monday. The company said it was a time-limited, voluntary program and built on insights gained from a previous voluntary retirement program. The eligible employees will receive details within the next few hours, it added.
